days.title: Why Verify? - Trust But Verify
days.learning_objective: Understand why verification is essential in an age of abundant information and AI-generated content.

days.title: Sources and Evidence - Where Information Comes From
days.learning_objective: Learn to identify and trace the sources of claims, understanding the chain from origin to you.

days.title: Primary vs Secondary - Getting Closer to the Truth
days.learning_objective: Distinguish between primary sources (original) and secondary sources (interpretations), and know when each is appropriate.

days.title: The Two-Source Rule - Cross-Referencing Everything
days.learning_objective: Apply the practice of confirming important information through at least two independent sources.

days.title: When AI Is Wrong - AI Can Hallucinate Confidently
days.learning_objective: Recognize that AI can generate plausible-sounding but completely false information, requiring verification.

days.title: When Experts Are Wrong - Everyone Makes Mistakes
days.learning_objective: Understand that even experts can be wrong, and healthy skepticism applies to all sources.

days.title: When You're Wrong - Catching Your Own Errors
days.learning_objective: Develop practices for checking your own thinking and catching your mistakes before they cause harm.

days.title: Confirmation Bias - Finding What You Want to Find
days.learning_objective: Recognize confirmation bias—the tendency to seek information that confirms existing beliefs—and counteract it.

days.title: Checking Your Bias - Awareness of Your Own Filters
days.learning_objective: Develop awareness of personal biases that filter what information you notice and believe.

days.title: The Chain of Evidence - Tracing Claims to Origins
days.learning_objective: Practice following claims back to their original sources, identifying where information may have been distorted.

days.title: Red Flags - Warning Signs of Bad Information
days.learning_objective: Identify common red flags that suggest information may be unreliable: sensationalism, lack of sources, emotional manipulation.

days.title: Reliable Sources - Characteristics of Trustworthy Information
days.learning_objective: Learn the characteristics that make sources more reliable: expertise, transparency, methodology, accountability.

days.title: Evaluating Websites - Is This Source Credible?
days.learning_objective: Apply evaluation criteria to websites, including checking authorship, bias, purpose, and publication standards.

days.title: Evaluating People - Is This Person Credible?
days.learning_objective: Assess the credibility of individual sources based on expertise, track record, and potential conflicts of interest.

days.title: Evaluating AI - Is This AI Output Accurate?
days.learning_objective: Develop specific strategies for verifying AI-generated content, including fact-checking and logical consistency.

days.title: Fact vs Opinion - Distinguishing Objective and Subjective
days.learning_objective: Clearly distinguish between factual claims that can be verified and opinions that reflect personal judgment.

days.title: Data vs Anecdote - Numbers vs Stories
days.learning_objective: Understand when statistical data is more reliable than personal stories, and when stories capture truths data misses.

days.title: Correlation vs Causation - Connected Doesn't Mean Caused
days.learning_objective: Avoid the common error of assuming that because two things are correlated, one causes the other.

days.title: Sample Size - Why Small Samples Mislead
days.learning_objective: Recognize that small samples can produce misleading conclusions, and look for adequate sample sizes.

days.title: Recency Bias - New Isn't Always Right
days.learning_objective: Recognize the tendency to favor new information over established knowledge, and evaluate appropriately.

days.title: Historical Accuracy - Checking Old Claims
days.learning_objective: Apply verification practices to historical claims, understanding that old doesn't mean accurate.

days.title: Scientific Consensus - When Experts Agree (and When They Don't)
days.learning_objective: Understand the value of scientific consensus while recognizing that science also evolves and updates.

days.title: Updating Beliefs - Changing Your Mind with New Evidence
days.learning_objective: Develop the habit of updating beliefs when presented with convincing new evidence, avoiding entrenchment.

days.title: Intellectual Humility - Being Wrong Well
days.learning_objective: Cultivate the ability to acknowledge mistakes gracefully and learn from being wrong.

days.title: Healthy Skepticism - Questioning Without Cynicism
days.learning_objective: Balance skepticism with openness—questioning claims without becoming cynical about all information.

days.title: Verification Tools - How to Check Facts
days.learning_objective: Learn to use fact-checking websites, reverse image search, and other verification tools effectively.

days.title: When to Verify - What Matters Enough to Check
days.learning_objective: Develop judgment about when verification is worth the effort based on stakes and consequences.

days.title: Teaching Verification - Helping Others Think Critically
days.learning_objective: Practice teaching verification skills to others, reinforcing your own understanding.

days.title: Verification in Daily Life - Applying Skills Everywhere
days.learning_objective: Apply verification habits to everyday information consumption, from news to social media to conversations.

days.title: Month in Review - The Practice of Verification
days.learning_objective: Consolidate the month's verification skills into a sustainable daily practice.

days.title: Verification Challenge - Test Your Skills
days.learning_objective: Apply all verification skills to a practical challenge, demonstrating critical thinking in action.
